questions.stem: Diamond and graphite are both forms of carbon, yet diamond is extremely hard while graphite is soft and slippery. What explains graphite's softness?

options.text: Graphite has weaker covalent bonds than diamond
Graphite's layers are held together by weak intermolecular forces, allowing them to slide over each other
Graphite contains fewer carbon atoms than diamond
Graphite is a simple molecular substance

questions.explanation: Graphite has a layered structure where each layer is a sheet of carbon atoms in hexagonal rings with strong covalent bonds. However, the forces between the layers are weak intermolecular forces, allowing layers to slide over each other easily, making graphite soft and useful as a lubricant. Diamond has a 3D network of covalent bonds in all directions.

questions.stem: Why do giant covalent structures have very high melting points?

options.text: They contain ionic bonds throughout the structure
Many strong covalent bonds must be broken throughout the entire structure
They have very strong intermolecular forces
They contain metallic bonds that are difficult to break

questions.explanation: Giant covalent structures consist of a continuous network of atoms held together by strong covalent bonds in all directions. To melt the substance, a large number of these strong bonds must be broken, which requires a huge amount of energy. There are no separate molecules, so there are no intermolecular forces to consider.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not. Why can graphite conduct?

options.text: Graphite contains ions that can move
Each carbon atom in graphite forms only 3 bonds, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that can move and carry charge
Graphite has a lower melting point so electrons move more easily

questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom forms 3 covalent bonds (not 4 as in diamond), leaving one outer electron per carbon atom delocalised. These delocalised electrons can move along the layers to carry electrical charge, similar to the free electrons in metals. In diamond, all 4 outer electrons are involved in bonding, so there are no free electrons.

questions.stem: Silicon dioxide (SiO₂) has a very high melting point of 1713°C and does not conduct electricity. What type of structure does it have?
questions.explanation: SiO₂ has a giant covalent structure similar to diamond. Each silicon atom is covalently bonded to 4 oxygen atoms, and each oxygen is bonded to 2 silicon atoms, forming a continuous 3D network. The very high melting point results from the many strong covalent bonds that need to be broken. It does not conduct because all electrons are used in bonding.

questions.stem: In diamond, each carbon atom forms bonds with how many other carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon atom forms 4 strong covalent bonds with 4 neighbouring carbon atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement. This is because carbon has 4 outer electrons, each of which forms a bond. This rigid 3D structure with bonds in all directions makes diamond the hardest natural substance. In graphite, each carbon forms only 3 bonds.
